introduction_markdown: Answer BOTH sections in the SAME answer booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Begin with SECTION A. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. In the Directed Writing question avoid indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer because this will earn you no marks. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Time allowed: two hours.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (e.g. your name, school, parentage etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Choose Picture B (family watching an aeroplane at an airport) and say so.
2. Introduction: link the picture to a personal event, an elder brother's return.
3. Preparation and journey to the airport.
4. Waiting, the landing and the meeting.
5. Conclusion: the lesson about the joy of reunion.

**Model composition (453 words)**

Picture B shows a family standing on the terrace of an airport, watching an aeroplane come down onto the runway. That picture reminded me of the day my family went to receive my elder brother, Ayuk, who was returning home after four years of study abroad.

The whole house had been awake since four o'clock that morning. Mother, who had cooked his favourite dish of ndole and plantains the night before, kept checking the clock. Father wore his best suit, and my little sister, Mimi, clutched a small paper flag she had made for the occasion. My aunt, who had wept with joy when she heard the news, put on her finest wrapper. We hired a taxi and drove to the airport, singing and laughing all along the road. Even the driver, who had never met Ayuk, joined our songs.

When we arrived, the terminal building was already crowded. A smiling officer told us that the flight from Paris was expected at ten o'clock, so we climbed to the terrace to watch the planes. The wait seemed endless. Mimi asked a hundred times, "When will Ayuk come?" and Father patiently replied, "Very soon." Meanwhile we watched other aeroplanes take off and land like giant silver birds, and the control tower stood tall in the distance.

At last, a loud roar filled the sky. A large aeroplane appeared above the trees, with its wheels lowered, and glided slowly toward the runway. We stood close to the rail, holding our breath. "That is it!" Father shouted. Mother pressed her hands against her chest and whispered a prayer. As the wheels touched the ground, we clapped and shouted with joy, and a few strangers around us joined in.

The next hour was the longest of my life. We rushed down to the arrival hall and waited behind a barrier while passengers came out one by one with their trolleys and bags. Then I saw him, taller and thinner than I remembered, wearing glasses and carrying a heavy bag on his shoulder. "Ayuk!" I screamed. Mimi ran forward and jumped into his arms, and Mother, tears streaming down her face, held him for a long time without saying a word. Father shook his hand, then hugged him tightly like a child, and his eyes shone with pride.

On the way home, Ayuk told us stories about the snow, the trains and the lonely nights he had spent studying. He had brought gifts for everybody, but the greatest gift was himself. That day I learnt that the joy of reunion makes every long separation worth the pain, and I shall never forget the sight of my family standing together on that terrace, with eyes lifted to the sky.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. No clear link with the picture chosen, or not saying which picture is used.
2. Describing the picture line by line instead of building a composition from it.
